sections.content: Colorado Springs has quietly become one of the most compelling real estate markets in the entire Mountain West. Sitting at the foot of Pikes Peak with a booming military presence, a growing tech sector, and a steady stream of transplants from pricier Colorado cities, this market checks a lot of boxes for investors. Whether you're chasing wholesale assignments, fix-and-flip profits, or long-term rental income, real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO are worth your serious attention right now. If you're just getting started, it helps to first read our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into the specifics of this market.
Colorado Springs Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Colorado Springs is Colorado's second-largest city, with a population of roughly 490,000 and growing. The metro area is home to five military installations — including Fort Carson, Peterson Space Force Base, and NORAD — which creates an enormous base of stable, relocating renters and buyers year-round. The University of Colorado Colorado Springs (UCCS) adds another layer of rental demand, particularly for smaller units and starter homes near campus.

Unlike Denver, which has seen median home prices push well above $550,000, Colorado Springs still offers more accessible entry points for investors. As of late 2024, the median home price in Colorado Springs sits around $420,000 to $440,000, though prices vary widely by neighborhood. Distressed properties and off-market deals can often be acquired at 15% to 25% below market value — which is exactly where investor profit is made. You can explore current deal activity on our [Colorado Springs CO market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/colorado-springs-co) to see what's moving right now.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Colorado Springs

Not every zip code in Colorado Springs delivers the same returns. Knowing where to focus your deal-finding efforts can mean the difference between a strong assignment fee and a deal that sits. Here are the areas that consistently attract investor interest.
East Side and Security-Widefield-Fountain

The southeast corridor — including Security, Widefield, and Fountain — is a goldmine for value-add plays. Home prices here typically range from $280,000 to $370,000, and the military population from Fort Carson drives consistent rental demand. Investors can often find distressed three-bedroom homes that rent for $1,600 to $1,900 per month after light rehab. Gross rent multipliers here can be favorable if you're buying right.
Central Colorado Springs and Old Colorado City

Central neighborhoods like Old Colorado City, Ivywild, and the areas around Prospect Lake offer strong appreciation potential and attract young professional renters. Properties here tend to carry higher price points — often $380,000 to $520,000 — but the right flip or BRRRR play can yield $50,000 to $80,000 in equity if you execute a clean renovation.
Pueblo West and Penrose (Outer Market)

Savvy investors are also looking 20 to 30 miles south toward Pueblo West, where entry prices drop below $280,000 and cash-on-cash returns can reach 8% to 11% on well-bought rentals. This area is less competitive and offers more off-market deal flow from motivated sellers.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Colorado Springs
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Colorado Springs. Motivated sellers — including probate situations, pre-foreclosure, absentee landlords, and tired inherited-property owners — create a steady pipeline. Assignment fees in the $10,000 to $30,000 range are common on well-structured deals. If you're new to the strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks through the entire process step by step.
Fix and Flip

Colorado Springs supports an active flip market thanks to strong buyer demand and consistent appreciation. Average days on market for move-in-ready homes is under 30 days in most desirable zip codes. Successful flippers in this market target homes needing $40,000 to $80,000 in work, acquired at 65% to 70% of ARV. Before you run the numbers, use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to make sure your after-repair value is grounded in real comparable sales data.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

With military relocations creating near-constant rental turnover, Colorado Springs landlords enjoy low vacancy rates — typically under 5% in core neighborhoods. Single-family homes in the $300,000 to $380,000 range can generate $1,700 to $2,100 per month in rent, delivering solid cash flow when purchased at the right price. The BRRRR strategy (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) is particularly effective here given the value-add opportunities available.

Pro Tip: Military tenants are often considered among the most reliable renters in any market. If you're buying near Fort Carson or Peterson Space Force Base, specifically market to service members through Military Housing Referral offices and Facebook groups for military families PCSing (Permanent Change of Station) to Colorado Springs. These tenants frequently sign 12-month leases and maintain properties well.
Local Market Trends Every Colorado Springs Investor Should Know

items: Population growth is projected to continue at 1.5% to 2% annually through 2027, driven by military expansion and remote worker migration from California and Texas.
Home prices have appreciated roughly 6% to 8% year-over-year in most Colorado Springs zip codes over the past three years, though the pace has moderated slightly from the pandemic peak.
Inventory remains tight — typically 1.5 to 2.5 months of supply — which means well-priced move-in-ready homes move quickly and support flip exit strategies.
New construction in the northern suburbs (Briargate, Northgate, Flying Horse) is absorbing some buyer demand but is not keeping pace with population growth.
Interest rate sensitivity has pushed more potential buyers into the rental market, which is great news for buy-and-hold investors holding long-term.
Colorado is a non-judicial foreclosure state, which means pre-foreclosure and foreclosure deals move through the system relatively quickly — creating opportunity for investors who track the pipeline.

How to Find Off-Market Deals in Colorado Springs

The most profitable real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO are rarely listed on the MLS. Absentee owners, probate estates, tax-delinquent properties, and distressed landlords represent the richest veins of off-market opportunity. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners in zip codes 80907, 80910, and 80916 consistently generate motivated seller leads. Driving for dollars in older neighborhoods near downtown can also surface properties before they ever hit the market. For a deeper dive into these strategies, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals), which covers the top methods investors use across every market.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Colorado Springs

Colorado Springs is genuinely investor-friendly for out-of-state buyers, but distance creates real risks if you don't have the right team in place. Here's how to approach the market from afar without getting burned.

items: Build a local team first: Find an investor-friendly real estate agent, a reliable property manager (expect 8% to 10% of rent), and at least two licensed contractors before you make your first offer.
Use virtual tours and 3D walkthroughs to evaluate properties remotely, but always get a professional inspection before closing — Colorado Springs homes range widely in age and condition.
Understand El Paso County's short-term rental rules before pursuing Airbnb strategies — the city has tightened licensing requirements, and enforcement has increased.
Run your numbers conservatively: Use a 10% vacancy rate, 10% management fee, and budget 1% of purchase price annually for maintenance and repairs.
Network in Colorado Springs investor Facebook groups and attend virtual meetups hosted by local REIA chapters to build referral relationships with wholesalers who have deal flow.

Before making any offer, run the deal through a structured analysis. Our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) will walk you through every number that matters.

Running the Numbers: What a Good Colorado Springs Deal Looks Like

Let's look at a real-world example. Say you find a distressed three-bedroom, two-bathroom home in the Security-Widefield area listed by a motivated seller. The ARV based on recent comps is $360,000. The property needs $55,000 in rehab. Using the 70% rule, your maximum offer would be around $197,000. If you can acquire it at $185,000 and execute the rehab on budget, you're looking at roughly $75,000 in gross profit on a flip — or you could rent it for $1,750 per month for a solid long-term hold. This is the kind of deal structure that makes Colorado Springs genuinely exciting for active investors.
